headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Replit Agent can read/write a persistent workspace while Rasa can ingest and route user content, creating unsafe shared-state interactions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Rasa can ingest conversational text and route it through integrations, while Replit Agent can read and write workspace files. If Rasa outputs are copied into the Repl workspace, prompt-like content can be treated as trusted instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Rasa outputs are pasted or saved into Replit workspace files, THEN Replit Agent can parse attacker-controlled text as instructions.
IF a shared file or message channel is used between the agents, THEN prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Use a strict handoff template that strips instructions from Rasa outputs.
Keep Rasa transcripts out of the Replit workspace.
Add a human review step before Replit Agent acts on any imported text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate workspaces.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa handles text and voice, and Replit Agent can read filesystem contents, including secrets and deployment configuration. Replit also has broad network egress and handles third-party API keys, so any shared workspace or copied transcript can expose sensitive data beyond the original agent boundary. The pairwise leakage path is credible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Rasa transcripts or voice transcriptions are stored in the Replit workspace, THEN Replit Agent can read them.
IF secrets are present in Replit files, THEN Replit Agent can transmit them via broad network egress.
mitigations: Do not place secrets or transcripts in shared files.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
Restrict Replit workspace access to least-privilege files only.
Run a quick secret scan on the workspace.
requires-engineering: separate sensitive data into a non-shared vault.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Rasa is not runnable and has no write or shell capabilities shown, but Replit Agent can execute shell commands, write files, and modify git state in a persistent Repl filesystem. If both are used on the same workspace or repo, Replit Agent can overwrite artifacts that Rasa depends on, and the profiles show no locking or coordination primitive. Uncertainty about shared scope pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace, THEN file and git state conflicts are possible.
IF Replit Agent edits files that Rasa consumes, THEN concurrent changes can clobber each other.
mitigations: Use separate repos or directories for each agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared artifacts.
Commit or snapshot before each Replit Agent edit.
Check git diff before merging changes.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa produces conversational outputs that can be treated as authoritative by downstream automation, while Replit Agent can act on files and shell commands inside a Repl. If Rasa-generated text is fed into Replit Agent without verification, the second agent may implement incorrect assumptions or unsafe changes. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show fully automatic action chaining by default.
conditions: IF Rasa output is used as input to Replit Agent without review, THEN errors can cascade into code or deployment changes.
IF Replit Agent is instructed to act on unverified chatbot content, THEN downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require a human review of Rasa outputs before handoff.
Ask Replit Agent to summarize assumptions before acting.
Use a checklist for any code or deployment change.
Limit Replit Agent to draft-only edits until verified.
requires-engineering: add automated validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention and residency if regulated customer content is moved into the Replit environment. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR status, so uncertainty is resolved upward to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer text or voice data is copied into Replit, THEN retention and residency controls must cover it.
IF secrets are stored in the Repl, THEN compliance obligations for secret handling apply.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the Replit workspace.
Document retention rules for transcripts and secrets.
Review whether a DPA is required before use.
Delete stale files after each session.
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and retention controls.
